children: Arabica coffee futures on ICE fell on Tuesday after hitting a six-week high, as hedging by farmers and profit-taking by speculators took the steam out of the market.
COFFEE
Arabica coffee
settled down 4.4 cents, or 1.4%, at $3.113 per lb​​, after earlier setting the highest price since September 9 at $3.1820​.
"Arabica futures took a break from the rally, and trade was mixed through the session. Producer selling and profit-taking came in at 310–315," said StoneX broker Tomas Araujo.

Market participants are looking at new arrivals of arabica coffee lots to ICE warehouses for possible increases in the certified stocks. There was a small increase in lots pending grading, but nothing significant.
Cepea/Esalq research said Brazilian coffee is already setting fruits in some areas, ahead of time, in a sign of uneven crop development.
Robusta coffee
settled down $56, or 1.6%, at $3,424 a metric ton.
SUGAR
•	Raw sugar
​​settled down 0.05 cent, or 0.2%, at 20.52 cents per lb.
* Dealers said the market looks sideways, after hitting a 19-month peak of 21.29 last week. Funds are holding a record long position, so they say the market is prone to a correction.

* Analyst Michael McDougall said Brazilian mills likely lost another 1 million tons of sugar production in the first half of October due to rains, increasing the lost production for the season to 5.7 million tons.

* The global sugar market supply deficit, or the gap between production and demand, was projected on Tuesday to grow to 6.28 million tons, 3 million tons more than a previous estimate, according to market analyst Green Pool Commodities.
* White sugar
was little changed at $547.10 a ton.
COCOA
London cocoa
​settled up £65, or 1.5%, to £4,445 per ton.
"Prices continue their sideways trading... last week’s better-than-expected grind was not a breakout catalyst," said broker StoneX in a note.
Dry weather across most of Ivory Coast's cocoa belt last week raised concerns about potential damage to pods for next year's harvest, farmers said.
New York cocoa
rose 2% to $5,801 a ton.
